messages:
Maria Chen: heads-up — noticed a weird mismatch between per-endpoint p99 and the service rollup for /v1/generate. per-endpoint p99 ~120ms, rollup p99 ~250ms. dashboard screenshot in comments.

Jon Patel: hmm that gap is pretty big. are we comparing the same time window and sampling?

Maria Chen: yes, same 15m window, same aggregation window. I pulled endpoint view: 
```
/v1/generate - p50: 18ms, p95: 46ms, p99: 120ms, count: 12.4k
service rollup - p99: 250ms, count: 126k
```
(rollup count includes other endpoints, but we filtered to the service and same tag set)

Tess Morrison: could be route-splitting/weighting during rollout. we recently split traffic across variants (v1,v2) with different latency profiles. rollup aggregator uses tdigest with uniform sampling per-shard — that can bias when shards have different volumes.

Alejandro Ruiz: remembered we added per-route sampling for quotas last week. if the telemetry sampler for rollups is downstream of routing, it might preferentially sample heavy slow routes. can you paste the rollout config?

Maria Chen: rollout policy attached (copied): 
```
route: /v1/generate
variants:
  - name: v1
    weight: 0.7
  - name: v2
    weight: 0.3
sampling: reservoir: 1000 per-shard
```

Samir Khan: ops-bot: recent telemetry-aggregator deploys?

ops-bot: telemetry-aggregator v3.14 deployed 1767777600. config: tdigest merge mode=default, per-shard reservoir=1000.

Jon Patel: that's the likely culprit. tdigest merge is not associative with weighted routes if sampling isn't proportional to traffic. when one route has heavier tail it skews the merged p99.

Tess Morrison: options: (1) switch rollup to compute per-route p99 then take weighted percentile approximation (we already do per-route p50/p95), (2) bias sampler to be proportional to route traffic, (3) increase reservoir and accept cost.

Alejandro Ruiz: for quick fix we could surface both rollup.p99 and max(per-route.p99) in the dashboard so product teams see the divergence. UX idea: show a little warning if rollup.p99 > max(route.p99)*1.2.

Maria Chen: +1 on warning. dashboard owners — would that be straightforward?

Tess Morrison: should be small frontend + backend change. backend already computes per-route percentiles for routing rules; expose max-per-route.p99 as a field in the rollup response. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4123 (draft)

Samir Khan: i'll add a unit test that simulates two shards with skewed tdigest samples to make sure we detect divergence. also will add a telemetry alert: if rollup.count differs from sum(route.count) by >5% or p99 divergence > 30% create a ticket automatically.

Jon Patel: long-term we should move toward deterministic rollup semantics: either do exact mergeable histograms (hdr) or make sampling proportional with route weights. both have tradeoffs. open a design ticket?

Tess Morrison: opened DOC-215: "Percentile semantics for rollups during route splits". assigned to eng-platform.

Maria Chen: thanks all. immediate action: Tess will land PR for dashboard warning, Samir will add test + alert, Jon/Alejandro will scope hdr vs sampler change for next sprint. tagging @eng-oncall in case this causes dashboards to flip during the rollout. :thumbsup:

Alejandro Ruiz: FYI i put an entry in the release notes so support doesn't get surprised if p99s move during the fix.

Maria Chen: resolved for now, will follow-up after the PRs land.
